searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; two left unspent. One shared search, restricted to the consorzio's domain, settled the eleven village units, their use on Gran Selezione alone and the nine tenths Sangiovese of the production code. Eleven were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain (antinori.it four times, ricasoli.com once, chianticlassico.com once, fontodi.com twice, montevertine.it three times, isoleeolena.it once) and are read as primary through their summaries. One search on Flaccianello's making returned nothing on the wine and was spent for nothing. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; nothing that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).
The searches went first to the dates, the people, the making and the label, then to the claims of a first; a fact the Codex library states stood on the library unless a search contradicted it.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a claim rested on one account, or was a report of one vintage, it was softened, turned into the typical case or cut.

Sources whose title or address names a living person (an interview headed with the Ricasoli heir's name, a Decanter piece headed with the Isole e Olena winemaker's name, a wine wiki under a writer's first name) were read in the results but never cited.

tested: The guild of 1385 and the palace of 1506: WineNews and the Italian Wikipedia give Giovanni di Piero Antinori in the Arte dei Vinattieri in 1385 and Niccolò di Tommaso Antinori buying the palace in 1506; one timeline gives 1461, which is the palace's building: confirmed, the forebears rightly described.
Giacomo Tachis: 4 November 1933 to 6 February 2016 in several accounts, at Antinori from 1961: confirmed.

The vintages: the 1970 a Chianti Classico Riserva Vigneto Tignanello with Canaiolo, Trebbiano and Malvasia, aged in small oak; the 1971 a Tuscan table wine named Tignanello; the white grapes gone in 1975; the blend of about four fifths Sangiovese, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc since 1982; no wine in 1972, 1973, 1974, 1976, 1984, 1992 or 2002 (the house's historical data): confirmed.

The house's firsts: its words are the first Sangiovese aged in small barrels, the first modern red blended with non traditional varieties such as Cabernet, and among the first Chianti Classico reds without white grapes: the record's softened Cabernet claim misquoted the house and was replaced by its white grape claim.

The site: south west facing at 350 to 400 metres on Pliocene marine marl rich in limestone with alberese, between the Greve and Pesa valleys (the house's estate and product pages); the address listings give San Casciano in Val di Pesa, not Mercatale: place and sites changed.

The making: destemmed and hand sorted (2009 and 2011 sheets), 15 to 20 days of maceration (2010), malolactic in small barrels, French oak with a smaller share of Hungarian for 12 to 18 months across vintages, about a year in bottle (2022): confirmed, the new oak cut.
The house rules: nobody living named; no price or score; no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

tested: The sheets of Castello di Brolio: vineyards at 400 to 490 metres in the later sheets and 250 to 450 in the 2011; the three soils, macigno, galestro of the Scaglia Toscana and alberese of Monte Morello; steel at 24 to 27 degrees Celsius with 14 to 16 days on the skins; 18 to 23 months in 500 litre tonneaux, 30 per cent new; about four months in bottle: confirmed but for the six vineyards, found nowhere, and the heights, which vary by sheet.

The village unit: the house's own page titles the 2020, 2021 and 2022 Gran Selezione Gaiole and the 2019 without it; the consorzio gives eleven units, on Gran Selezione alone: the label line changed to the 2020.

The first vintage: the house's 1997 sheet (eighteen months in barriques, bottled in June 1999) and a merchant's page calling the 1997 the first vintage of the estate's new flagship: restored to the story.

The sale and the return: the sale of the brand to Seagram dated to the 1960s in one account and the early 1970s in another, the family keeping the castle and the vines; the brand later with Hardy's; bought back in 1993 (Montecristo Magazine, Wine Spectator's obituary of the later baron): confirmed, around 1970 kept.

The letter of 1872: to Cesare Studiati of the University of Pisa, dated 26 September 1872 in one account, the consorzio's own milestone calling it the Iron Baron's first recipe; the exact proportions disputed: confirmed as a view, the proportions rightly left out.
The rules: Gran Selezione with Sangiovese at nine tenths or more in the production code; the eleven units (the consorzio): confirmed.
The house rules: the vintage by vintage blends and the recent vintages in classification, grapes and others turned to the typical case; the living heir not named.

tested: The purchase of 1968, the terracotta and the organic certificate: the house's own pages give the family's hands since 1968, its terrecotte tiles, certified organic; roof tiles found nowhere: changed to tiles.
The Conca d'Oro: the house says the golden shell for its amphitheatre shape; travel accounts trace the gold to the wheat grown there before the war: the story hedged and the card given both.

The first vintage and the label: 1981 by Decanter and Grape Guru, 1980 by one merchant; Colli della Toscana Centrale IGT on the label (Vino.com's address and Decanter): confirmed, 1981 kept with the library.

The single vineyard and the selection: 2001 by Decanter and a merchant's note on the 2001, the single vineyard until 2004 by Wine Watch, Vigna del Sorbo kept out of the selection: the date widened to early in the 2000s.

The making: wild yeasts and at least three weeks in steel (Leon and Son, 2021), 24 months in barriques and French oak barrels (2021), 18 months for the 2014 by a critic, 24 for the 2008, Allier and Tronçais (Vino.com), the barrel time rising from 12 to 24 months and later vintages finishing in 25 hectolitre casks (Decanter): the barrique time widened and the larger casks added; temperature control and malolactic in barrel found nowhere, cut.
Vigna del Sorbo as a Gran Selezione around 2000: anachronistic, since the tier was approved in 2013; changed.
The house rules: the label's in one family's hands since 1968 is a present claim of ownership, turned into history; the founder's son and the consultant of 1981 met as living names and kept out.

tested: The purchase of 1967 by a steel industrialist as a holiday house, two hectares planted, the first vintage of 1971 sent to Vinitaly through Siena's chamber of commerce (the house's own page); Wine Spectator's obituary gives 1968 for the purchase: 1967 kept with the house and the library.

The first Le Pergole Torte of 1977, the first Sangiovese alone vinified in the Radda zone by the house's own words, from historic vineyards planted between 1968 and 1999: confirmed; the story no longer draws the 1977 from the one vineyard.
The vineyard: Le Pergole Torte planted in 1968, two hectares, facing north north east; the estate at 425 metres; organic since the 2009 vintage (the house's pages): confirmed.

The making: glass lined cement vats without temperature control, two pump overs a day, 20 to 25 days, malolactic in cement, a year in Allier barriques and a year in Slavonian casks, about three months in bottle (the house's page and 2020 sheet): confirmed.

The exit: Chianti Classico Montevertine from 1971 to 1981 and plain Montevertine from 1982 after leaving the consorzio (the house); 1981 tied to the white grapes in several accounts, 1982 in one: kept.
The labels: a woman's face by an artist friend, the series dated from 1982 in one account: the 1980s kept.
The house rules: the founder (died 2000) and the artist described; the living son and the taster of the house's early years kept out.
